In SaaS, the mantra of "build it and they will come" no longer works. Customer expectations are higher than ever before, and in an age when anyone can vibe code a basic app in hours for free, your app has to be amazing to be worth a monthly subscription.

You can scatter yourself in a million directions, but the smartest thing you can do to make your SaaS app valuable is simple: just listen. Collecting customer feedback leads to higher customer satisfaction, lower churn, more revenue and less wasted time.

Customer feedback tools help you automate this process and collect feedback quickly, even with a large user base.

Today, we look at some of the top tools for collecting qualitative and quantitative feedback from SaaS users. 👇

TL;DR - here are the best choices

1. ✨ Featurebase - Best overall modern tool for feedback, bug reports, and surveys
2. Hotjar - Best for session replays and heatmaps
3. SurveySparrow - Best for enterprise-level surveys, costs a lot
4. UserVoice - Best enterprise feedback collection and prioritization
5. Usersnap - Best for customizable feedback widgets
6. Typeform - Best for advanced forms and surveys
7. Qualaroo - Best for timed in-app surveys, outdated UI
8. Mopinion - Best for website feedback, expensive
9. Zonka - Best for measuring CX and surveys
10. InMoment - Best for digital listening, enterprise tool
11. AskNicely - Best for reputation management and surveys, most expensive
12. featureOS - Best for simple feedback collection with basic boards and roadmaps, but limited prioritization
13. Usersnap - Best for capturing visual feedback and bug reports directly from users with screenshots
14. Canny - Best for structured feature request management with voting and prioritization
15. Userpilot - Best for in-app onboarding combined with surveys and product usage insights

## What is a SaaS feedback tool?

A SaaS customer feedback tool is a platform that lets you collect feedback from your software users. These platforms let you gather feedback in various shapes and forms, such as:

- Feature requests
- Bug reports
- NPS, CSAT, and customer effort score surveys
- Qualitative feedback on user behavior
- In-app feedback
- And others

Collecting (and acting on) customer feedback will increase customer satisfaction and lifetime value, lower your churn, and ultimately increase your revenue.

In-app feedback widget example (live demo)

User feedback tools automate the most tedious tasks in collecting feedback, such as running interviews, contacting customers through email, translating qualitative feedback into measurable insights, and more.

In essence, good customer feedback software is always not a cost but an investment in customer satisfaction.

## Top features that SaaS feedback tools should have

Before we go into tools that help you capture feedback from your users, let's set the foundations first. These are the features you should look out for in your next feedback tool.

- Customizable feedback forms (that support custom fields, so you can ask for additional info like product category for the feature requests, browser version for bug reports, etc.)
- Integrations for feedback collection (Intercom, Slack, Discord, etc.)
- Feedback tagging and categorization (AI-powered topic identification, sentiment analysis, adding tags to most common topics)
- Product roadmaps (or, at the very least, integration capabilities with roadmapping tools)
- Integrations with issue trackers (e.g., development and project management tools such as Jira, Linear, and Clickup)
- User segmentation (the ability to segment users by revenue, new vs. returning customers, headcount, industry and more)
- Anonymous feedback options (the ability to submit user feedback without logging in and authenticating)
- Features for closing the feedback loop automatically (to send emails and update customers when their feedback item is rejected, worked on, or completed)
- Real-time analytics data and reporting (to get insights on who is leaving feedback, where, and what the feedback says)
- Customer feedback surveys (with templates and most common formats, such as NPS (Net Promoter Score), CES, and CSAT)+ a whole range of other more advanced features to understand user interactions and get actionable user feedback.
- Support conversations are one of the richest feedback sources you have, which is why SaaS customer support and feedback collection work best when they're connected.

The best customer feedback tools have all or most of these features, but finding the right one requires extensive research, especially the pricier ones. Let's take a look at the very best user feedback tools in the market. 👇

## Best SaaS feedback tools to try in 2025

If you don't want to miss out on valuable user feedback, these tools can help throughout different platforms and situations.

### 1. Featurebase ✨

Featurebase's feedback forum

Featurebase (👋 that's us) is an affordable all-in-one feedback tool that lets you collect, analyze, and act on feedback. It offers a modern interface with customizable forums and feedback widgets.

Some of the many features that Featurebase offers include:

- Fully customizable customer feedback portal with feature voting
- Public product roadmaps
- In-app feedback widget
- Surveys (NPS, CSAT, etc)
- Grouping and analyzing user feedback with AI features
- Anonymous feedback and a variety of authentication options for existing users
- Product changelog with an in app popup option
- Help Center
- Integrations with Linear, Intercom, Jira, Slack, Zapier and many other tools
- And all of this in 40+ different languages

In short, you get all the tools in one place to gather detailed feedback, sort and analyze it, create tasks for your developers in your favorite project management app, get the work done, and communicate this back to your users.

Featurebase comes with a free plan and affordable pricing starting from $29 per user per month. You can try all paid plans with a 10-day free trial.

### 2. Hotjar

Hotjar screen recording preview

How do you measure customer satisfaction if you want to track what people do with your product? Hotjar is one of the best qualitative feedback apps in the game. It allows you to record the screens of your users as they are in the app, as well as create heatmaps with frequently used portions of a page.

Some of its top features include:

- Heatmaps to reveal customer insights on user experience and user interface
- Screen recordings of individual app users
- Customer surveys
- In-app feedback button
- 1:1 customer interviews

Prices start at $32 for tracking up to 100 sessions per day, but you can also get a free plan with limited features and up to 35 daily sessions. It's one of the most popular customer support tools in 2026, with a strong focus on qualitative feedback.

### 3. SurveySparrow

SurveySparrow survey dashboard.

You can use surveys to ensure better customer retention and capture quantitative and qualitative feedback data. And when simple tools like Google Forms don't cut it, SurveySparrow is one of the best paid alternatives.
